positive: Compact or contiguous high-temperature region at a burn pile with visible contemporaneous flame or smoke evidence.
Persistent ember or residual burn-pile heat after visible flames diminish, when temporal continuity and scene location establish the same fire event.
negative: Warm ground, roof, vegetation, person, vehicle, reflection, or equipment without fire-event evidence.
Bright region whose relation to a fire event cannot be determined from source footage and context.
annotation_guidance: Draw around the visibly fire-related hot region, not the whole colored thermal background or camera overlay.
Separate spatially distinct burn sites; do not join multiple targets in one box solely because both are bright.
If a small detached bright speck may be an ember or unrelated hot object, flag ambiguous rather than forcing a label.
Do not infer T/V same-target identity from timestamp alone; visible and thermal fields of view differ.
rationale: The experiment explicitly evaluates residual hotspots; treating a confirmed smoldering burn site as negative in late frames would create time-dependent contradictory labels. Brightness alone is insufficient for a positive.
needed_confirmation: Review late-frame source-video continuity and target identity for every proposed residual-heat positive before creating the derived validation split.
